rewrites.//: SPA fallback. The negative lookahead keeps /api/* and the real static assets from being rewritten to index.html — without it a missing API route would return an HTML document with a 200, which is far harder to debug than a 404.

headers.//: Keep in sync with public/_headers and the nginx block in Dockerfile.

headers.value: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://fonts.googleapis.com; font-src 'self' https://fonts.gstatic.com; img-src 'self' data: blob:; connect-src 'self'; worker-src 'self' blob:; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; object-src 'none'

headers.//: Hashed build output is content-addressed, so it can be cached forever.

The service worker is NOT hashed and controls every request in the demo. A cached copy would keep serving stale mock handlers after a deploy, so it must be revalidated every time. Service-Worker-Allowed lets it claim the root scope.
index.html is the SPA entry point and references hashed assets; it must never be served stale.
